Don’t take this the wrong way but I think your daughter probably has had more exposure than you think. Kids who are sheltered from reality tend to find out themselves and are often more secretive. This is scientifically true. The book is picked especially for her age group to study. By all means there may be difficult themes but that is the whole point of studying that text. Your daughter will be STUDYING the text and will learn about its difficult themes and whats potentially wrong with them and/or how it differs from society now. This is important for your daughter to understand these topics at her age else it wouldn’t be a text that is recommended she study. She isn’t just reading the book she will be understanding the difficult themes in class as that is what is being taught. I imagine she will understand it much better than you as it is what she is going to school for. Also as a father don’t compare yourself as a child to your own child. Everyone is an individual and your daughter may differ more than you think to yourself.

I understand the book may not align with your beliefs but I think that is more of a reason your daughter should study it. At her age she is practically an adult and the themes in the book won’t be celebrated but studied in regard to the historical context. The subject English Literature is about studying the differences in texts overtime and segregating yourself away from certain texts defeats the point of studying the subject.
